newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate firm despite weekend factor.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate firm despite weekend factor.

text.p: * Market volume higher at 21.28 bln from 7.03 bln pesos
Philippine interbank call loan rates were firm on Monday at an average of 10.28125 percent despite the covering of weekend positions, traders said.
Banks continue to enjoy ample liquidity even after remitting billions of pesos of tax payments last week, dealers said.
Rates moved in a tighter band from 10.25 to 10.28125 percent, with 32 lenders and 22 borrowers. In secondary market trading of T-bills, sellers continued to swamp the market but buyers were scarce.
"Why should they buy T-bills at the present level when rates are expected to go up," a foreign bank dealer said.
"Buyers would rather wait for the auction," a dealer said.
T-bill rates are seen rising at the auction later today after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate last Friday by 0.25 percentage-points to 10.25 percent.
The Central Bank lifted its rate to align it with the domestic trend and to quell an attack on the peso.
A Reuters poll of six banks gave offer rates of 10.25 to 10.40 percent on the three-month bills; 10.55 to 10.70 on the six months; and 11.25 to 11.45 on the one-year bills.
